program_note:
The Bird of Paradise, the official flower of the City of Los Angeles, is an immigrant—like many of Los Angeles’ residents.  Its jazzy and contrasting colors and repeating rhythms is a perfect metaphor for this city of the future, constantly reinventing and re-emerging from itself.  The upward angle of the flowers conveys a yearning to fly up to the heavens, reflected in the arcs and repeating rhythm of the leaves.  But the flower is also spiky and sharp, and may hide some secrets!

Written for the Los Angeles Chapter of the American Harp Society’s “Los Angeles Celebration of the Harp: New Music Competition,” the composition is approximately eight minutes in duration.

David S. Lefkowitz

May, 2014
